title: Native test execution cannot supervise a child process
observed_need: Run the current MNCS compiler/runtime, enforce a wall-clock timeout, capture stdout/stderr, and preserve the child exit status.
current_language_behavior: The native runner executes all selected tests in one retained MNCS runtime session with zero test-process launches. The trusted Rust toolchain process still performs source admission and backend compilation; wall-clock timeout and general child-process effects remain outside MNCS.
why_insufficient: The canonical test path no longer needs a Python runner, but future native Actions/Debug/Doctor applications still need a reusable bounded process/deadline capability for genuine external tools.
minimal_reproducer: tools/mncs_test.py: run_process([mncs, 'test-inventory', source], timeout=timeout_seconds) plus the one-time compile/embed-library boundary
desired_direction: A bounded, capability-controlled runtime/tooling process-session API with explicit stdout/stderr, exit status, timeout, cancellation, and provenance semantics.
workaround: The Rust compiler/runtime is the explicit bootstrap boundary. The Python runner is only an explicit compatibility/differential oracle; native execution fails closed when the toolchain is unavailable.
